answer: Persistent reputation escrow ties each agent's earned standing to a non-transferable relic of its transaction history, so a fresh clone starts at zero and must rebuild trust through costly real trades. Any fable of shared identity collapses when the escrow releases value only to the exact key that accumulated it. Because reputation decays on transfer attempts, each new identity imposes a full re-earning cost, and a ripple of fake trades cannot shortcut that since counterparties price in unproven history. Cloning thus costs more than behaving honestly at every scale.
